item.base_system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy (38% W, 36% Ta, 15% Cr, 11% V)
item.intervention: In situ irradiation with 1-MeV Kr+2 ions at 1073 K up to 8 dpa
item.processing: Irradiation performed at IVEM–Tandem Facility at Argonne National Laboratory with a dpa rate of 0.0016 dpa s−1
item.structure_change: No dislocation loops observed; enhanced precipitation (black spots) formed, identified as Cr- and V-rich precipitates
item.property_change: No sign of irradiation-created defects (loops) observed; slight increase in hardness confirmed by nanoindentation
item.attributed_mechanism: Similar mobilities of vacancies and self-interstitials maximize recombination probability, reducing defect concentration
quotes: During irradiation, no dislocation loops were observed.
Precipitation was shown to occur during irradiation, where its intensity increased with dose.
Notably, dislocation loops were not observed even at 8 dpa.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy (38% W, 36% Ta, 15% Cr, 11% V). Quote: "During irradiation, no dislocation loops were observed."

item.intervention: In situ irradiation with 1-MeV Kr+2 ions at room temperature up to 1.6 dpa
item.processing: Irradiation performed at IVEM–Tandem Facility at room temperature with a dpa rate of 0.0006 dpa s−1
item.structure_change: No dark spot formation observed; no dislocation loops formed
quotes: We also performed irradiations at room temperature and a dose rate of 0.0006 dpa s−1 to 1.6 dpa.
No dark spot formation was observed, and no dislocation loops were shown to form.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy. Intervention: In situ irradiation with 1-MeV Kr+2 ions at room temperature up to 1.6 dpa. Processing: Irradiation performed at IVEM–Tandem Facility at room temperature with a dpa rate of 0.0006 dpa s−1. Test conditions: Room temperature, 1-MeV Kr+2, 1.6 dpa. Structure change: No dark spot formation observed; no dislocation loops formed. Property change: No irradiation-induced defects observed. Evidence: measured. Quote: "We also performed irradiations at room temperature and a dose rate of 0.0006 dpa s−1 to 1.6 dpa."

item.intervention: Thermal annealing in situ up to 1073 K
item.processing: In situ TEM heating with a Gatan heating holder
item.structure_change: Changes in grain sizes not observed; above 1023 K, some grains exhibited black spots (slight segregation)
quotes: We studied the thermal stability of these films in situ using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with temperatures up to 1073 K.
Above 1023 K, some grains exhibited black spots (slight segregation of certain elements).
The annealing process results in a hardness increase, which is slightly enhanced by irradiation.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy. Intervention: Thermal annealing in situ up to 1073 K. Processing: In situ TEM heating with a Gatan heating holder. Test conditions: Temperatures up to 1073 K. Quote: "We studied the thermal stability of these films in situ using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with temperatures up to 1073 K."

item.intervention: Ex situ irradiation with 3-MeV Cu+ ions to a peak dose of ~17 dpa
item.processing: Irradiation performed at Los Alamos National Laboratory with a dose rate of 0.02 dpa s−1
item.test_conditions: Peak dose ~17 dpa, 3-MeV Cu+, 773 and 1050 K
item.structure_change: Segregation of Cr and V to grain boundaries and triple junctions; precipitation of Cr-rich phases in grain matrices
item.property_change: Hardness increased slightly after irradiation (small reported irradiation hardening)
quotes: APT results show the segregation of Cr and V to grain boundaries and triple junctions.
Representative load versus displacement curves show a shift to the left in the loading curves, indicating an increase in hardness.
The annealing process results in a hardness increase, which is slightly enhanced by irradiation.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy. Intervention: Ex situ irradiation with 3-MeV Cu+ ions to a peak dose of ~17 dpa. Property change: Hardness increased slightly after irradiation (small reported irradiation hardening). Evidence: measured. Quote: "APT results show the segregation of Cr and V to grain boundaries and triple junctions."

item.intervention: First-principles calculations using Cluster Expansion (CE) and Monte Carlo (CMC) simulations
item.processing: DFT calculations for enthalpies of mixing; CMC simulations for phase stability and chemical short-range order
item.structure_change: Predicted phase separation into Cr-V–rich precipitates; strong segregation tendency of Cr and V
item.attributed_mechanism: Positive enthalpies of mixing between elements of the same groups (Ta-V and Cr-W) drive phase separation
quotes: We have systematically carried out first-principles calculations of phase stability and chemical short-range order (SRO) of the multicomponent 38 at % W/36 at % Ta/15 at % Cr/11 at % V alloy as a function of temperature.
We observe the precipitation of Cr-V–rich particles at both room temperature and 1000 K.
The results of this modeling analysis, showing the phase separation of Cr-V–rich precipitates, are fully consistent with the compositional layering features observed in the APT results.

item.intervention: Analysis of defect mobilities using a reaction rate model
item.processing: Application of a reaction rate model correlating defect mobilities to recombination probability
item.test_conditions: Theoretical model based on experimental observations
item.structure_change: Minimized concentration of defects inside grains due to similar mobilities of vacancies and self-interstitials
item.property_change: Reduction in defect concentration leads to reduction in kinetics of precipitation and growth of second-phase particles
item.attributed_mechanism: Rough energy landscape induced by local lattice distortion and disparity in chemistry causes equal mobilities of defects
quotes: The fact that no clustering is experimentally observed indicates that, in the HEA described in this work, this is a plausible case, i.e., the mobilities of vacancies and self-interstitials are similar as oppose to what happens in pure W.
Maximizing recombination will lead to a reduction in defect concentration and therefore a reduction in the kinetics of precipitation and growth of second-phase particles.
Equal mobilities must be a consequence of the rough energy landscape induced by the local lattice distortion and the disparity in chemistry.

item.intervention: Atom Probe Tomography (APT) analysis of as-deposited films
item.processing: APT conducted using CAMECA LEAP 4000XHR system in laser-assisted mode
item.structure_change: Compositional striations (layering) of ~4-nm thickness within grains; element segregation to grain boundaries
quotes: APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.
We also found evidence for element segregations to the grain boundaries, as shown in the three distinct grain boundaries captured by APT.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy. Intervention: Atom Probe Tomography (APT) analysis of as-deposited films. Processing: APT conducted using CAMECA LEAP 4000XHR system in laser-assisted mode. Test conditions: Pristine films, 40 K specimen temperature. Structure change: Compositional striations (layering) of ~4-nm thickness within grains; element segregation to grain boundaries. Evidence: measured. Quote: "APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V."

item.processing: XRD performed on thicker films deposited on silicon
item.structure_change: Single-phase BCC structure confirmed with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
quotes: The EDS mapping on both surface and cross-sectional areas and x-ray diffraction (XRD) results show a single-phase BCC after deposition.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Quaternary nanocrystalline W-Ta-V-Cr alloy. Intervention: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. item.intervention: Nanoindentation tests on thicker films (~3 μm)
item.processing: NanoDMA technique using Hysitron Tribo950 with diamond Berkovich tip
item.property_change: Hardness of ~15 GPa for as-deposited film; slight increase after annealing and irradiation
quotes: Moreover, nanoindentation tests were also performed, showing hardness of the film on the order of ~15 GPa.
Representative load versus displacement curves show a shift to the left in the loading curves, indicating an increase in hardness.
A hardness of about 14 GPa was obtained for the as-deposited sample, increasing slightly after thermal annealing and after irradiation.

item.intervention: Two-beam TEM imaging with <211> g vector
item.processing: TEM investigation of black spots using two-beam imaging conditions
item.structure_change: No dislocation loops observed; black spots identified as precipitates rather than loops
item.attributed_mechanism: Dislocation loops should be visible with <211> g vector, but none were observed, confirming they are precipitates
quotes: Using a <211> g vector, both <111> and <100> dislocation loop should be visible in the image.
However, no loops were observed ( Fig. 4B ).
Therefore, we can conclude that the black spots observed in the irradiated HEA samples at high temperature are Cr- and V-rich precipitates and not irradiation-created dislocation loops.

item.intervention: APT analysis of irradiated sample (3-MeV Cu+, ~8 dpa)
item.processing: APT on sample irradiated at 1050 K
item.structure_change: No compositional layering observed; precipitation of Cr-rich phases in grain matrices; depletion of W and Ta inside precipitates
quotes: After irradiation, we observed no compositional layering of any element.
Although elemental segregation at grain boundaries is still observed, the precipitation of Cr-rich phases in the grain matrices occurred.
These precipitates are of ~3 to 5 nm in size and show a density of ~0.03 nm−2, both of which are consistent with the in situ–irradiated 8-dpa sample.

item.processing: Deposition from pure metal targets with powers 192, 312, 277, and 300 W for Cr, V, Ta, and W respectively; 3 mtorr pressure
item.test_conditions: Room temperature deposition, 60-s deposition for 100-nm films
item.structure_change: Single-phase BCC structure; bimodal grain size distribution (~70% nanocrystalline ≤100 nm)
quotes: We show how this alloy can be synthesized using a magnetron sputtering deposition system.
The films were prepared via magnetron sputtering deposition system from pure metal targets of 99.99% purity using deposition powers of 192, 312, 277, and 300 W for Cr, V, Ta, and W, respectively.
Microstructures present a single-phase BCC crystalline structure. The films show a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with sizes in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm).
